jobs.title: Chief of Staff to CEO
jobs.description:
About Treeswift

In the face of rising threats, increasing pressure on affordability, and unprecedented demand for power, Treeswift empowers energy companies to modernize their field work to meet the growth and challenges ahead.

We build physical AI for the field worker: whether on foot or in a vehicle, our technology is an ironman suit for engineers, linemen, and vegetation crews: same worker, same boots on the ground, now operating at 10x productivity. Our platform is powered by cutting edge hardware, sensors (LiDAR, camera, etc…), AI and software designed to revolutionize work in the toughest environments.

Since our first pilot with a utility in June 2024, we've grown fast, now working with three of the five largest utilities in the US. To date, our technology has enabled our customers to reduce wildfire risk, regulatory and outage risk from vegetation, avoid delays and cost overruns in new construction, and accelerate recovery from severe storms.

To tackle this challenge, we are bringing together a team of mission-driven experts with deep industry experience in robotics (Penn, Caltech, CMU) and enterprise software development (Palantir, Stripe, Oracle, MongoDB). We have raised funding from leading investors including Penny Pritzker’s Inspired Capital.

We are headquartered in midtown Manhattan, with additional offices in San Francisco and Philadelphia.

Our growth is only accelerating. We’re looking for deeply curious and highly ambitious people who want to have a real world impact. Come build the future of (field) work with us.

The Position

We're hiring a Chief of Staff to work directly alongside our CEO as a true extension of their judgment, network, and execution. This is not an administrative or project management role; your primary objective is to increase the leverage of the CEO as a strategic operator. That means building and managing executive relationships across the utility industry, ensuring the CEO is spending time with the right people at the right moments, and developing a deep enough understanding of Treeswift's business and strategy to help the CEO drive the company's most important priorities internally.

You'll own the operating cadence around the CEO's external relationships, proactively identifying who they should meet, orchestrating introductions, managing outreach, preparing them for conversations, and ensuring follow-up actually happens. You'll also step in to represent the CEO credibly in front of clients and partners and own high-priority strategic projects that cut across the company. Internally, you'll help the CEO turn company strategy into action, working across sales, operations, engineering, and leadership to surface issues, drive decisions, and make sure the highest-priority work moves forward. This person will often be the CEO's stand-in in external-facing conversations, and needs to build trust with technical, operational, and executive audiences alike.

This role requires someone who naturally operates with high agency. We want someone who notices what should happen next and makes it happen without waiting for direction.

If you're energized by building relationships, thrive in ambiguous environments, and want a front-row seat to building one of the world's leading physical AI companies, we'd love to talk.

What You'll Do

Multiply the CEO's effectiveness

Own the CEO's external operating system, including outreach, relationship management, meeting preparation, follow-up, and long-term engagement strategy
Proactively identify opportunities for the CEO to deepen relationships with utility executives, board members, investors, and strategic partners
Build and maintain a structured pipeline of executive relationships, ensuring important conversations happen before they're needed
Manage the CEO's calendar strategically, optimizing for long-term company outcomes rather than simply filling available time
Prepare concise, thoughtful briefs before important meetings, including background, objectives, recommendations, and follow-up actions

Build executive relationships

Become a trusted face of Treeswift within the utility industry
Develop relationships with utility executives, industry leaders, advisors, and strategic partners
Attend conferences, customer meetings, and industry events to expand Treeswift's network and identify new opportunities
Coordinate executive introductions, dinners, customer visits, and relationship-building opportunities
Ensure no important relationship goes stale by maintaining thoughtful, consistent follow-up

Drive Company Operations And Strategic Initiatives

Own cross-functional strategic projects end to end that directly support the CEO and executive team
Coordinate board materials, fundraising preparation, strategic partnerships, and special projects
Run executive operating rhythms, leadership meetings, planning sessions, and company-wide initiatives
Identify bottlenecks before they become problems and drive them to resolution
Serve as the connective tissue across leadership, ensuring priorities stay aligned and execution stays on track

Communicate on behalf of the CEO

Draft communications on the CEO's behalf, including board updates, investor narratives, internal memos, and company-wide announcements
Prepare materials for board meetings, fundraising conversations, and strategic reviews
Serve as a connective layer between the CEO, the leadership team, and the broader company

Who You Are

You genuinely enjoy meeting people and building long-term professional relationships
You probably already know people across the utility ecosystem, or you have a demonstrated ability to quickly build credibility in executive circles
You have an MBA or comparable experience in consulting, investing, strategy, or startup leadership
You instinctively manage up. You don't wait to be told what to do next. You anticipate what the CEO will need before they ask.
You're highly organized without becoming bureaucratic. You build systems that make execution easier.
You communicate exceptionally well, both verbally and in writing. You'll frequently write on behalf of the CEO and represent Treeswift externally.
You're comfortable speaking with everyone from frontline operators to Fortune 500 CEOs.
You have excellent judgment. You know which problems deserve the CEO's attention and which can be solved independently.
You can move between strategy and execution without missing a beat.
You have high agency: you spot what needs to happen and go do it, rather than waiting for direction
You're excited about physical AI, robotics, or infrastructure/utilities, and energized by the idea of learning a genuinely technical business well enough to operate credibly within it
You thrive in ambiguity and enjoy solving problems that don't come with a playbook.
You care deeply about building enduring companies and want to help define the future of AI for field workers. That means helping Treeswift become deeply embedded with utility leaders as it scales its expansion strategy.
You thrive in ambiguity and are comfortable with the pace and scope-shifting of an early-stage company. No two weeks in this role will look the same

What We Offer

Competitive salary and equity package
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your eligible dependents
Life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage
16 weeks of fully paid parental leave to support all new parents
Flexible, unlimited paid time off
401(k) retirement savings plan
Free OneMedical membership
Commuter benefits
Snacks, goodies, and team lunches provided twice a week to keep you fueled and connected with your colleagues.

What We Value

Mission first. We value team members who are focused on working towards the best outcomes for the customer and the business.
Curiosity. We are constantly learning – from each other and from our customers.. We aren’t afraid to learn we were wrong in the process and adapt our approach accordingly.
Owners mindset. If you see an opportunity for improvement, run with it. We believe that good ideas can come from anywhere, no matter your role.

The estimated base salary range for this role is $160,000 to $195,000. Final compensation is determined by skills, experience, qualifications, and location, and does not include the value of any bonuses, benefits, or long-term incentives. This range is disclosed in compliance with the New York City Human Rights Law and applies to NYC-based roles. Compensation may vary for candidates located outside of New York City.

Treeswift is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We provide employment opportunities without regard to age, race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, disability, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other protected status in accordance with applicable law.

If you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, whether it be alternate forms of material, accessible meeting rooms, etc., please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

jobs.title: Senior Director of Advocacy
jobs.description:
Brief Description

Summary of Position:
The Senior Director of Advocacy will provide strategic leadership to advance Connection’s goals to increase affordable housing in Illinois through state, county, and municipal policy advocacy. The Senior Director will lead the policy and advocacy team, driving strategy and methodology, manage day-to-day operations, build operational structures and processes, leverage technology to expand organizing capacity, and deepen a culture of cross-departmental collaboration. The position drives the vision and methodology to substantially expand volunteer municipal chapters that work to affect local housing policies, with the technical support of Connections’ advocacy staff, and leverages chapters in support of state policy campaigns. The Senior Director supervises a team of staff including a Director of Public Policy and two Associate Directors.

Specific Duties

Organizing and Leadership Development (60%)

Oversee the development and implementation of an organizing framework and strategies that build a volunteer chapter network across northeastern Illinois to advance municipal policies that create more affordable housing.
Build the technology infrastructure needed to facilitate organizing, direct policy actions, and leadership development of advocates.
Develop annual goals that align with agency priorities that result in sustainable expansion of impact.
Guide the development of a comprehensive library of affordable housing trainings to be used for general education, advocate identification, and chapter development and organizing skills.
Consistently develop the housing policy acumen of the municipal team to effectively support local advocates in advancing affordable housing policy.
Oversee the development of strategies to engage internal stakeholders including clients, staff, and volunteers in policy advocacy efforts including supporting our participant advisory board and staff advocacy committee.
Engage with elected officials, advocacy groups, and community leaders to promote housing affordability and homelessness solutions.
Build out data tracking processes to measure outputs and impact of policy and advocacy work and ensure consistent and timely reporting.
Oversee the full utilization of advocacy CRM to enhance impact and grow advocate engagement and development.

Policy (20%)

Set strategy and oversee the development of the agency policy platform and ensure the timely delivery of an annual policy agenda.
Build a vision to engage municipal chapters in policy agenda priorities.
Provide strategic counsel to the CEO and executive leadership team on emerging policy and advocacy opportunities, risks, and strategies.
Ensure the development of strategies to cultivate relationships with government officials at all levels of government and effective tracking and reporting systems to keep executive leadership informed of relationship cultivation status.
Ensure the development of effective research and data collecting and analysis strategies to drive innovative policies, provide evidence-based solutions, and build a repository of best-practice policy templates.
Identify and implement opportunities for the organization to raise its national and regional profile.
As a lobbying compliance officer, ensure adherence to agency policies and protocol that support lobbying recordkeeping and reporting. As needed, engage in lobbying activities.

General Responsibilities (20%)

Develop and manage staff, providing leadership, and coaching to achieve departmental goals.
Build operational structures that facilitate efficient, effective results and ensure transparency of work output to executive leaders.
Ensure efficient planning and execution of all policy and advocacy events in collaboration with key internal stakeholders.
Assist in developing funding proposals and reports and collaborate with CEO and development to cultivate funder relationships, raising the profile of the organization across the region.
Develop and manage department budget and ensure department adherences to finance protocols.
Build effective relationships with organizational leaders to ensure cross-departmental collaboration, leveraging resources and information to advance the mission of the organization.
Ensure team compliance with agency policies and standards.
Maintain and strengthen Connections’ relationships with external advocacy partners, coalitions, and policymakers.
Represent Connections externally at key policy, advocacy, and coalition meetings, advancing organizational advocacy priorities.
Collaborate with communications team to set comprehensive marketing and communications strategy to advance policy and advocacy goals.
Provide staff leadership for the advocacy committee of the Board of Directors.
Adhere to the Code of Conduct for Connections for the Homeless.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Requirements

The following qualifications are requirements for the position:

Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in advocacy, public policy, government relations, community organizing, or a related field, including a minimum of 5 years of leadership and people management experience.
Experience utilizing technology to amplify movement building and influence power over decision makers.
Demonstrated success in managing teams with staff at different levels of an organization.
Experience in evaluating program outputs and impact.
Strong external relationship-building, coalition engagement, and public advocacy skills.
Bachelor's degree or higher in public policy, nonprofit management, political science, urban planning, or a related field or equivalent experience.
Valid driver's license, proof of insurance, and reliable transportation to travel throughout the region as needed to perform essential job duties.

The Following Qualifications Are Highly Desirable

Deep knowledge of affordable housing, homelessness policy, and community-based advocacy.
Experience with a federated advocacy model.
Experience developing and mobilizing people with lived experience.
Familiarity working with Boards of Directors and executive leadership teams.
Experience with lobbying regulations and reporting requirements.
Experience with budgeting and fiscal management.

Other Requirements

Must submit to a criminal background check and provide evidence of a recent tuberculosis test.
Must be able to work evenings and weekends as necessary to support advocacy initiatives and stakeholder engagement.

Summary

For nearly 40 years, Connections for the Homeless has served and catalyzed our community to end homelessness, one person at a time. Each year we provide eviction prevention, shelter, and housing services to 4,000 people from across north suburban Cook County. Beyond providing direct services we also operate a robust advocacy and community organizing program to address the root causes of homelessness. The COVID pandemic accelerated our growth in the depth and breadth of services we offer and the organizational infrastructure to sustain this highly impactful organization. Connections is a radically reshaped organization deeply committed to demonstrating our core values in all relationships with participants, colleagues, donors, partners, and volunteers.

Join our dedicated team at Connections for the Homeless, where we blend a commitment to making a difference with a competitive rewards package. Our full-time employees enjoy a range of benefits, consciously crafted through an equitable lens, to support their well-being and professional growth.

At Connections for the Homeless, we recognize that supporting our employees is essential in achieving our mission. We are ready to invest in you as you make a difference in our community. We can't wait for you to join us!

jobs.title: Executive Director - Catonsville
jobs.description:
Overwhelmingly, people who decide they want to be a part of the Y in Central Maryland tell us they do so because it reflects their values and a conscious decision, they’ve made about how they choose to live their lives. The happiest and most fulfilled Y associates are those who are motivated to help others and who want to be a part of something larger than themselves. If this speaks to your heart, then we invite you to join our team. Be a part of a charitable, mission-driven organization that works for individual and community well-being for all, for a better us.

At the Y in Central Maryland, we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being and professional growth. Enjoy flexible schedules, competitive pay, and generous paid time off, alongside medical, dental and vision benefits, as well as dependent care FSA. We offer a generous employer contribution to the Y retirement fund, and opportunities for career advancement. Our commitment to fostering a positive work environment means you'll have access to training and development programs that align with our mission to empower individuals and strengthen communities. Join us and bring your passion to a fulfilling career where you can truly make a difference!

How This Role Contributes To The Y’s Mission

As a Y Executive Director, you will be responsible for the daily operations of one or more Y Family Centers. You will provide leadership in the areas of associate hiring, supervision and development, volunteer management, fiscal management, financial development, membership and program administration, facility & equipment stewardship, community relations and personal-professional development. You will develop, implement and monitor long range plans for the expansion of programs and services, in harmony with overall Y objectives. You will be responsible for leading and growing Family Center operations of 4,000+ household membership units and a combined budget of $2.5 million. As a Y Executive Director, you’ll contribute to the Y and to the broader community we serve by creating experiences that help people feel a greater sense of health and well-being, purpose, acceptance and belonging.

This Work Is Right For You If You Have

A love of wellness and people
At least five (5) years of prior experience successfully managing Health & Wellness, recreation, and youth programming field, preferably in a Y or similar organization
The ability to clearly communicate and effectively listen to children, parents/guardians, members, and other Y associates
Prior experience supervising a 4,000+ unit health & wellness center that provide services for all ages
A proven track record in business operations including producing growth and strong financial management
A bachelor’s degree in in a Human Services, Business Management, Business Administration or equivalent

All Y associates agree to abide by The Code of Conduct with Youth that sets clear expectations for associates and volunteers to ensure a safe and respectful environment for young people. It emphasizes treating youth with respect and fairness, avoiding inappropriate physical or verbal interactions, and adhering to established standards of affection. The policy strictly prohibits any form of abuse, bullying, or harassment and mandates the reporting of suspected mistreatment. Additionally, associates and volunteers must complete training on child abuse prevention and comply with legal reporting requirements to safeguard youth.
